## PCI PM callbacks reaching `i915_pm_suspend`

The i915 driver registers `i915_pm_suspend` as its normal system-suspend callback:

- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c:1718–1724`
  - `.suspend = i915_pm_suspend`

The PCI PM framework reaches it through these callback paths:

```text
pci_pm_suspend()
  → pm_generic_suspend()
    → driver->pm->suspend()
      → i915_pm_suspend(kdev)                 [i915_driver.c:1392]
        → kdev_to_i915(kdev)
          → i915 = struct drm_i915_private *
        → i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)        [i915_driver.c:1404]
```

For poweroff/hibernation:

```text
pci_pm_poweroff()
  → pm_generic_poweroff()
    → driver->pm->poweroff()
      → i915_pm_suspend(kdev)                 [shared suspend callback path]
        → kdev_to_i915(kdev)
        → i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
```

The direct i915 callback relationship indexed by codegraph is:

```text
pci_pm_suspend   → i915_pm_suspend
pci_pm_poweroff  → i915_pm_suspend
```

The i915 PM callback itself first handles the absent-device and switcheroo-off cases:

```c
struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);

if (!i915)
        return -ENODEV;

if (i915->drm.switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF)
        return 0;

return i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm);
```

  → i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)

i915_pm_freeze(kdev)
  → i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)

`i915_pm_suspend` itself is the normal callback that also invokes `i915_drm_suspend`.

## Callers that also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

None of the PCI PM callback paths that reach `i915_pm_suspend` also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`.

They are separate PM domains:

```text
System suspend:
pci_pm_suspend / pci_pm_poweroff
  → i915_pm_suspend
